newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-GARCION'S DOPING BAN REDUCED BY THREE MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GARCION'S DOPING BAN REDUCED BY THREE MONTHS.

text.p: Lille midfielder David Garcion had a doping ban reduced from nine months to six by the commission of appeal of the French Soccer Federation (FFF) on Wednesday.
Garcion, who failed a dope test for steroids at the end of a league match against Nice in December, had been given a nine-month ban at an initial hearing.
But commission members said they had reduced the sentence after Garcion insisted he had not knowingly taken the steroids.
"I'm the first real doping case in the history of French football. It was impossible not to punish me," said Garcion.
The suspension, which will mostly take effect at the start of next season, applies only to France but it could be extended at continental and world level by UEFA or FIFA.
The 23-year-old midfielder was transferred to Lille from Nantes on loan at the start of this season.
Previous doping cases that have come before the commission have all involved cannabis.
